script.title: Suspense Account in Rectification
script.caption_hook: Trial balance not tallying? Park the difference here!

lines.say: My trial balance doesn't tally. Do I just leave the difference?
No. We park the gap in a Suspense Account. It's a temporary account, used until we find the errors.
Park it? Like a scooter in a parking slot?
Exactly! Say the debit total is ₹49,500 and the credit total is ₹50,000. Debit is short by ₹500.
So Suspense goes on the debit side?
Yes. The short side gets the plug. Debit short, Suspense debit. Credit short, Suspense credit. No journal entry is needed for this.

board.title: Where Suspense goes
board.sub: Debit short: Suspense Dr; credit short: Cr

lines.say: Then how does that difference ever disappear?
We hunt for errors. A one-sided error upsets the trial balance. A two-sided error with equal debit and credit doesn't.
Then where do we fix two-sided errors?
Between the two accounts concerned. Suspense isn't used there.
Show me one example with Suspense.
Sales were credited ₹500 short. So debit Suspense ₹500, and credit Sales ₹500.
Oh! So Suspense becomes nil once all errors are fixed!
Exactly. Suspense is only a parking slot. The short side gets the plug.

check_notes: Checker: Lines 12–13 (example and its conclusion): the example doesn't match the set-up. In Lines 4–6, debit is short by ₹500, so Suspense gets a ₹500 DEBIT balance. Line 12 then corrects under-credited Sales with 'Suspense A/c Dr 500, To Sales A/c 500'. That debits Suspense a second time and leaves a ₹1,000 debit balance, so Line 13's 'Suspense becomes nil' is false. Sales credited ₹500 short would make the CREDIT side short, which gives Suspense a ₹500 credit balance. Fix: either (a) keep the debit-short scenario and use a debit-side error, e.g. 'Purchases were debited ₹500 short: Purchases A/c Dr 500, To Suspense A/c 500', which clears the ₹500 debit in Suspense; or (b) keep the Sales example and change Lines 4–5 to 'credit total ₹49,500, debit total ₹50,000, credit short by ₹500, so Suspense goes on the credit side'. Then 'Suspense A/c Dr 500, To Sales A/c 500' brings Suspense to nil.

Checker: Line 13: 'Suspense becomes nil once all errors are fixed' is true only if all the errors are corrected. With the example as written, it is wrong, as explained above. Make the example consistent so the nil balance actually follows.
